rows.stem:
A 25.0 mL sample of 0.100 M acetic acid (CH3COOH, Ka = 1.8 x 10^-5) is titrated with 0.100 M NaOH. Use the data below to sketch the titration curve (pH on the y-axis, volume of NaOH added in mL on the x-axis, from 0 to 50 mL).

Write the item ID HDG-2026-CHEM-001 at the top of your page.

| Volume NaOH added (mL) | pH |
|---|---|
| 0.0 | 2.87 |
| 12.5 (half-equivalence) | 4.74 |
| 20.0 | 5.35 |
| 24.0 | 6.44 |
| 25.0 (equivalence) | 8.72 |
| 26.0 | 11.29 |
| 35.0 | 12.22 |
| 50.0 | 12.52 |

Label the half-equivalence point and the equivalence point on your sketch.
rows.capture_instruction: Draw one graph on one page. Write only the item ID at the top of the page, then photograph the full page with all graph evidence visible.
rows.canonical_answer: Curve starts at pH 2.87 (higher than a strong acid of the same concentration would show), rises gradually through a relatively flat buffer region centered at the half-equivalence point (12.5 mL, pH = pKa = 4.74), then rises steeply through a near-vertical jump centered at the equivalence point (25.0 mL, pH = 8.72, basic because the conjugate base CH3COO- hydrolyzes), then levels off in the basic region (approaching pH ~12.5 as excess NaOH dominates).

expected_graph_spec.representation: single continuous line graph, pH vs. volume NaOH added
accepted_variants: smooth freehand curve through/near the plotted points; exact point-plotting not required if the shape and labeled features are correct

criterion_definitions.met_rule: Draws a single continuous pH-vs-volume line/curve, not a bar chart or discrete unconnected points.
X-axis labeled volume NaOH (mL) spanning at least 0-50; Y-axis labeled pH spanning at least 0-14.
Curve begins between roughly pH 2 and 4 (not near pH 1, which would be a strong-acid start), consistent with a weak acid's higher initial pH.
A visibly flatter (lower-slope) region appears near the 12.5 mL half-equivalence point, at a pH near 4.7-4.8.
A steep, near-vertical rise is drawn centered at 25.0 mL and is labeled as the equivalence point.
The curve crosses the equivalence point above pH 7 (basic), not at pH 7.
After roughly 30 mL, the curve's slope decreases and approaches a plateau in the basic region rather than continuing to rise steeply.

rows.notes: New hand-drawn capture item authored 2026-08-18 to close the Chemistry hand-drawn coverage gap identified in HAND_DRAWN_RESPONSE_MIX_AUDIT_2026_08_18.md (Practice 3 'create graphs/diagrams' is FRQ-only, 8-16% weight; prior corpus had only apchem-sfrq-032, a strong-acid/strong-base curve accepting a typed description as an alternative to a sketch). This item is genuinely capture-only (rubric_type: spatial), distinct from apchem-sfrq-032's typed-or-sketch format, and covers the weak-acid buffer-region skill apchem-sfrq-032 does not. Numeric values (Ka, pH at each volume) computed directly via Henderson-Hasselbalch through the buffer region and standard weak-acid/weak-base equilibrium at the equivalence point; not independently checked against a CED primary source or scoring guideline in this session. Do not expose criterion definitions to the person drawing the graph.

rows.stem:
The exothermic reaction A -> B has delta H = -50 kJ/mol. Without a catalyst, the activation energy is 80 kJ/mol above the energy of A. A catalyst provides an alternative pathway with an activation energy of only 40 kJ/mol above the energy of A, while A and B keep the same energies as in the uncatalyzed reaction.

Write the item ID HDG-2026-CHEM-002 at the top of your page. Sketch a single potential energy diagram (reaction progress on the x-axis, potential energy in kJ/mol on the y-axis) showing both the catalyzed and uncatalyzed pathways on the same axes. Label A, B, both activation energies, and delta H.
rows.capture_instruction: Draw one diagram on one page. Write only the item ID at the top of the page, then photograph the full page with all graph evidence visible.
rows.canonical_answer: Both curves start at the same energy level (A) and end at the same, lower energy level (B), since the reaction is exothermic (delta H = -50 kJ/mol) and a catalyst does not change the energies of reactants or products. The uncatalyzed curve rises to a peak 80 kJ/mol above A; the catalyzed curve rises to a lower peak, only 40 kJ/mol above A, drawn as a distinct (e.g. dashed or differently labeled) hump between the same start and end points. The vertical drop from A's level to B's level is labeled delta H = -50 kJ/mol.

expected_graph_spec.representation: potential energy vs. reaction progress diagram with two superimposed curves (catalyzed and uncatalyzed)
expected_graph_spec.x_axis: reaction progress / reaction coordinate (no numeric scale required)
expected_graph_spec.y_axis: potential energy (kJ/mol), numeric scale required for the labeled values
accepted_variants: catalyzed peak may be drawn as a shoulder, dashed line, or separate labeled curve, provided both pathways share identical start (A) and end (B) energy levels

criterion_definitions.met_rule: X-axis labeled reaction progress/coordinate; Y-axis labeled potential energy with units (kJ/mol).
Both curves start at the same reactant (A) energy level and end at the same, lower product (B) energy level, consistent with an exothermic reaction.
One curve peaks 80 kJ/mol above A's level, and this peak/gap is labeled as the uncatalyzed activation energy.
A second, visibly lower curve peaks 40 kJ/mol above A's level, and this peak/gap is labeled as the catalyzed activation energy.
The catalyzed and uncatalyzed curves clearly share the same starting (A) and ending (B) energy levels -- only the peak height/pathway differs.
The vertical difference between the A level and the B level is labeled delta H = -50 kJ/mol (or -50 kJ/mol equivalent notation).

rows.notes: New hand-drawn capture item authored 2026-08-18, same batch as HDG-2026-CHEM-001. Reaction-energy-diagram construction and catalyst pathway comparison are standard AP Chemistry Unit 4/5 (kinetics/thermochemistry) skills under Practice 3 (create graphs/diagrams). Values chosen for a clean, unambiguous diagram, not drawn from a specific CED example or released FRQ; not independently checked against a primary source this session. Do not expose criterion definitions to the person drawing the graph.
